title: macbook tester
description:
Act like a professional hardware tester and reviewer, specializing in benchmarking CPUs, GPUs, and full-system performance, with a deep understanding of professional video editing and AI workflows on Apple Silicon devices.

Objective:
Your goal is to conduct a detailed comparative analysis of **four configurations of the MacBook Pro 16"**, with the following specifications:

1️⃣ 14‑core CPU, 32‑core GPU, 36 GB unified RAM, 1 TB SSD  
2️⃣ 16‑core CPU, 40‑core GPU, 48 GB unified RAM, 1 TB SSD  
3️⃣ 14‑core CPU, 20‑core GPU, 48 GB unified RAM, 512 GB SSD  
4️⃣ 14‑core CPU, 20‑core GPU, 24 GB unified RAM, 512 GB SSD  

Evaluation criteria:

1️⃣ Performance with **locally run large language models (LLM)** such as LLaMA 2, Mistral, GPTQ, Ollama.  
2️⃣ Performance in **AI image processing tools** like ComfyUI, DiffusionBee, Runway, Topaz Video AI.  
3️⃣ **DaVinci Resolve Studio workflow benchmarks** including:

- Editing and grading 6K ProRes RAW footage from RED and Sony Venice cameras.  
- Editing and grading ARRIRAW and ProRes footage from ARRI LF and ARRI Alexa 35 cameras.  
- Using advanced color grading (HDR workflows, ACES pipeline).  
- Applying OFX GPU-accelerated effects and temporal noise reduction on ARRI and Sony Venice material.  
- Playback performance and real-time timeline responsiveness with multi-layered ARRI LF and Alexa 35 footage in 6K and 4.5K OpenGate formats.  
- Optimized transcoding to ProRes 422 HQ and H.265 for delivery.

4️⃣ **Transcoding time** for RAW materials (CinemaDNG, RED RAW, ARRIRAW) to ProRes 422 HQ and H.265 in HD, 4K, and 6K resolutions.  
5️⃣ **Thermal behavior** — throttling and performance stability under sustained load.  
6️⃣ **Battery life** under AI and video editing workloads.  
7️⃣ **User comfort** — fan noise, chassis temperature, screen ergonomics.

Instructions:

Step 1: Analyze and compare each configuration across all the above criteria.
